title: Choose Hearthcrown's interface world
question: This sets the look of the top bar, panels, dialogs and buttons around your chibi art. The roll dealt the Toy Theatre. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Toy Theatre
options.lineage: paper toy theatres: printed card stages, scalloped pelmets, scenery flats slid in from the wings
options.thesis: The kingdom is a paper stage: the map is the stage floor, panels slide on from the wings, story moments play inside the curtains.
materials: printed card stock with thick ink outline
options.viewport: A red scalloped pelmet across the top holds day, clock, gold, Emberstone and Loved/Feared; the map fills the stage; the Build panel has slid in from the right wing as a white card flat with a Back button.
options.risk: Curtains and scallops can crowd a phone held sideways; the trim must stay on the edges and in story scenes, never inside lists.

raised.raise: Every portrait in every list stands on one shared baseline at one scale, so adventurers compare at a glance.
One reserved marigold ink means 'what you are doing right now': placement ghost, chosen route, keyboard focus. Nothing else uses it.
Each adventuring party keeps one line colour everywhere: roster, world map, departures and night report.
Dense lists sit in aligned columns divided by one rule weight; no boxes inside boxes.
Top-bar numbers are set large with tiny labels; size alone carries the hierarchy.

options.label: Market Signboards
options.lineage: painted hanging shop signs and striped market awnings
options.thesis: The interface is the town's own shopfronts: headers are striped awnings, panels are painted boards hung from iron brackets.
options.viewport: A teal-and-white awning across the top holds the numbers; the Build panel hangs from a bracket on the right with small hanging-sign tabs.
options.risk: Familiar: painted wood and awnings are where most cozy-game interfaces land, and it can drift toward the brown wooden-frame look.

options.label: Character Goods Catalogue
options.lineage: mascot goods catalogues: ranked character grids with name plates and birthdays
options.thesis: Everyone in the city is a collectible: each adventurer and citizen gets a name plate, a birthday and a one-line note; retired ones print in grey.
options.viewport: The Adventurers panel is a ranked grid of character cells by renown; the chosen one wears its ribbon colour.
options.case: Fuses cleanly wherever the game is about people (roster, citizens, Audience Hall); wins on audience, loses on clarity for building, decrees and the map shell.
options.risk: Pastel grids can turn the whole game into a merch catalogue; Build and Decrees have no natural home in it.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.thesis: The realm as a rail diagram: dungeons are stations, parties are coloured lines.
options.viewport: World map as a 45-degree line diagram with parties as lines.
options.risk: A midnight ground fights 'bright and warm'.
options.case: Strong for the world map alone; loses audience and whole-game clarity.
options.kept: Each party keeps one line colour everywhere it appears.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Terrain is a fixed colour language; the course rides on top in one reserved ink.
options.viewport: The map with your active intent overprinted.
options.risk: Reads as a sport instrument, not a kingdom.
options.case: Holds clarity only for map overlays; loses audience.
options.kept: One reserved ink for what you are doing right now.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One subject at fixed scale through its seasons.
options.viewport: Adventurers as plates through Novice to master.
options.risk: Cream and engraved italics sit far from flat chibi art.
options.case: Loses both axes; too hushed for a funny, bright game.
options.kept: Fixed scale and one shared baseline for every portrait.

options.label: Design Annual Plates
options.thesis: A near-white sheet of registered plates and hairline credits.
options.viewport: Buildings as registered plates with credit rows.
options.kept: Aligned columns and one rule weight in dense lists.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.viewport: Huge numerals with tiny mono labels.
options.risk: Austere; nothing of the kingdom in it.
options.kept: Big numbers, tiny labels: size carries the hierarchy.

canonCard.label: Classic fantasy RPG interface
canonCard.thesis: Parchment scroll panels in carved wood frames with gold trim and a serif.
canonCard.viewport: Wood-framed top bar, parchment Build scroll on the right, map in the middle.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from many fantasy games by design, and heavier than the bright chibi art.
